source.label: Local Notion HTML export
source.note: All 25 exported HTML pages are published or explicitly accounted for. The canonical hub page and two linked chapters (Audience & Story, Applied Use Cases) were not part of the export; those destinations are editorial synthesis and are labelled as such.

chapters.title: Foundations
chapters.question: What decision is this chart for?
chapters.summary: Start with the question, the grain, and the variable types. Visualization is an evidence layer, not decoration — and summary statistics can agree while the data disagree completely.

chapters.title: Audience & Story
chapters.question: Who needs to act, and what do they need to see?
chapters.summary: The communication layer: name the audience, commit to one big idea, and connect evidence to a message and a decision. This chapter is editorial because the storytelling source pages were not included in the export.

lab.label: See context → action in a dashboard

chapters.title: Core Visual Grammar
chapters.question: Which encoding matches the analytical task?
chapters.summary: The six workhorse plots — histogram, box, scatter, line, bar, dot — plus the scale decisions that make them honest: bin width, zero baselines, log axes, and trend lines.

chapters.title: Advanced & Multivariate
chapters.question: How do you show a third variable without lying?
chapters.summary: Size and transparency are weak encodings. Faceting, pair plots, correlation heatmaps, parallel coordinates and polar views each answer a narrower question — and each has a failure mode.

chapters.title: Color & Perception
chapters.question: What job is color doing here?
chapters.summary: Qualitative, sequential and diverging palettes are not interchangeable. Color should carry meaning the position encoding cannot, and it must survive grayscale and contrast checks.

chapters.title: Accessibility & Color QA
chapters.question: Can the meaning survive without the color you chose?
chapters.summary: Labels, position, pattern and direct annotation before hue. Test contrast on text, marks and states, then run a grayscale check before publishing.

chapters.title: Integrity, Uncertainty & Traps
chapters.question: What would make this chart misleading?
chapters.summary: Truncated baselines, dual axes, chartjunk, and aggregation that hides the distribution. Then the inference traps that look like chart problems: Simpson's paradox, selection bias, multiple comparisons and uncertainty.

chapters.title: Decision Tools & Composition
chapters.question: Which chart, and how should the page be composed?
chapters.summary: A task-first selection matrix and the composition rules that turn charts into a dashboard: context, KPI, explanation, detail, action — with cognitive load treated as a design constraint.

chapters.title: Implementation
chapters.question: How do these principles survive inside the tool?
chapters.summary: The same decisions inside Power BI: measures versus calculated columns, high cardinality, interaction design, color, performance, and the log-axis caveat.

chapters.title: Practice, Assessment & Shelf
chapters.question: Can you defend the choice under pressure?
chapters.summary: Interview-style reasoning, a pre-publish checklist, reading paths, curated references, and applied cases. Favour trade-offs over trivia.

lessons.title: Library map & operating system
lessons.intro: The exported hub page. It defines the working pipeline, the canonical chapter spine, and the figure pack — use it as the map for everything else.
takeaways: The pipeline is question → decision → grain → variables → task → encoding → scale → context → integrity → action.
A chart is an evidence layer; storytelling is a separate communication layer.
Pick one job before you pick one chapter.

lessons.title: Foundations & Decision Framework
lessons.intro: Why plots exist, how to classify a variable, and the default decision framework used by every later chapter.
takeaways: Similar summary statistics do not imply similar data — plot it.
A variable's type is a property of the question, not just the column.
The chart is the last decision, not the first.

lessons.title: Audience, Big Idea & Action
lessons.intro: The exported corpus points to a separate storytelling library that was not included. This chapter is a short, clearly labelled editorial synthesis of the communication duties listed in the canonical map — it is not a transcription.
takeaways: Name the audience and the decision before choosing the evidence.
One big idea per view; everything else is supporting detail.
End with the action and the caveat, not with a decorative chart.

lessons.title: Core Chart Types & Scales
lessons.intro: The full reference for histogram, box, scatter, line, bar and dot — including bin width, log scales, trend lines and the mistakes each plot invites.
takeaways: Histogram bins are a design choice, not a default.
Bar length starts at zero; other marks do not automatically follow that rule.
A date on the x-axis is not a reason to connect the points.

lessons.title: Advanced & Multivariate Techniques
lessons.intro: Third variables, faceting, pair plots, correlation heatmaps, parallel coordinates, pie charts and rose plots — and when each is the wrong tool.
takeaways: Position before size or transparency when precision matters.
A correlation heatmap screens; it does not replace scatter plots.
Polar coordinates need a genuine cyclical question.

lessons.title: Color Theory for Data Visualization
lessons.intro: HCL, the three palette families, and why viridis is a practical sequential default.
takeaways: Nominal categories get a qualitative palette; ordered magnitude gets sequential.
Diverging needs a meaningful midpoint, not two pretty colors.
Test the palette in grayscale before trusting it.

lessons.title: Accessibility, Contrast & Color QA
lessons.intro: A short pre-publish QA pass: color independence, palette semantics, contrast, grayscale, and the interview answer that proves you actually test.
takeaways: Never use red/green alone to carry status.
Contrast applies to labels, gridlines and states — not just body text.
Run a grayscale check; if the message disappears, the encoding is too weak.

lessons.title: Visual Integrity, Pitfalls & Ethics
lessons.intro: Eight recurring pitfalls, then the axis and scale rules that prevent them: bar-length, stacking, dual axes, chartjunk and the visualization constitution.
takeaways: A truncated bar axis manufactures a difference that is not there.
Dual axes invent correlation through scale choice.
Minimalism means removing non-data ink, not removing context.

lessons.title: Statistical Interpretation Traps
lessons.intro: Many visualization failures are inference failures. Mean versus median, Simpson's paradox, ecological fallacy, selection bias and uncertainty.
takeaways: Check the denominator and the mix before celebrating a lift.
An aggregate trend can reverse inside every segment.
Statistical detection is not the same as a decision-sized effect.

lessons.title: Visual Atlas — Teaching Figures
lessons.intro: The figure pack behind the chapters: encoding strength, histogram shapes, baselines, palette families, KPI anatomy, dashboard scan paths and uncertainty.
takeaways: Use the atlas as a wall card, not a replacement for the reasoning.
Every figure isolates one decision you can point at in review.
Match the figure to the chapter before quoting it.

lessons.title: Chart Selection Matrix & Anti-Patterns
lessons.intro: The practical layer over the chart library: begin with the analytical task, then the data structure, then the simplest trustworthy encoding.
takeaways: Task first, chart second.
Prefer position on a common scale over angle, area or hue.
Name the hazard before you publish the view.

lessons.title: Dashboard Design & Cognitive Load
lessons.intro: Visual hierarchy, small multiples, KPI anatomy, and the difference between an executive and an analytical dashboard.
takeaways: The scan path Context → KPI → Explanation → Detail → Action is the design.
A KPI without window, target, direction and exception is incomplete.
Executive views reduce choices; analytical views add diagnostic depth.

lessons.title: Power BI Visualization Playbook
lessons.intro: The curriculum applied inside Power BI: measures, high cardinality, performance-aware visuals, interactions, color and log-axis caution.
takeaways: Measures aggregate at query time; calculated columns live in the model.
High cardinality needs Top N + Other, search or drill-through.
A log axis is a deliberate analytical statement, not a styling choice.

lessons.title: Interview Master Bank
lessons.intro: Conceptual, scenario, senior and rapid-fire questions drawn from the export. Answer with trade-offs, not definitions.
takeaways: Structure answers as context → goal → data structure → candidates → trade-off → risk → recommendation.
Correlation near zero rules out a linear association, not every relationship.
An outlier is a question, not an automatic deletion.

lessons.title: Quick Reference & Exam Prep
lessons.intro: The pre-publish checklist, comparison table, exam traps and the mental model that compresses the whole library.
takeaways: Run the checklist before defending the chart.
Know the trap pairs: bar vs line, histogram vs bar, mean vs distribution, dual axis vs panels.
Question → grain → variables → task → encoding → scale → context → integrity.

lessons.title: Applied Cases (synthetic)
lessons.intro: The canonical Applied Use Cases page was not included in the export. These four short cases are new implementation material built on disclosed synthetic data — not summaries of the missing page.
takeaways: Each case starts with a decision and a grain.
The chart is justified by the task, not by the domain.
Every synthetic figure is labelled and reproducible from the local dataset.

lessons.title: المدرج التكراري — Histogram
takeaways: عرض الـbin قرار تصميمي، وليس قيمة افتراضية.
افحص التعدد النمطي والالتواء قبل كتابة أي استنتاج.
المحور Y هنا عدّ، وليس قيمة فئوية.

lessons.title: مخطط الصندوق — Box Plot
takeaways: الصندوق يلخص الوسيط والربيعيات، وليس كل شكل التوزيع.
النقاط الشاذة تستحق التحقق، وليست خطأً تلقائيًا.
قارن المجموعات على مقياس مشترك.

lessons.title: مخطط التشتت — Scatter Plot
takeaways: افحص الشكل والتكتلات والقيم الشاذة قبل حساب الارتباط.
الارتباط لا يثبت السببية.
المحور اللوغاريتمي يحتاج تبريرًا وتحذيرًا واضحًا.

lessons.title: الرسم الخطي — Line Plot
takeaways: وجود التاريخ على المحور X لا يجعل الرسم الخطي مناسبًا تلقائيًا.
الخط يعني أن الملاحظات متصلة مفهوميًا.
النمو الأسي يبدو خطيًا على مقياس log — اقرأ المحور.

lessons.title: مخطط الأعمدة — Bar Plot
takeaways: طول العمود يجب أن يبدأ من الصفر.
الترتيب حسب القيمة يسهّل المقارنة.
لا تخلط بين Bar وHistogram.

lessons.title: مخطط النقاط — Dot Plot
takeaways: النقاط أفضل من الأعمدة عند المقارنة على مقياس log.
يمكن عرض عدة مقاييس على نفس الفئة.
اقرأ اتجاه المحور اللوغاريتمي قبل الحكم على الحجم.

lessons.title: الرسوم الأساسية — Univariate & Bivariate
lessons.intro: صفحة فهرس عربية تربط دروس الرسوم الستة. استخدمها كنقطة بداية للمسار العربي.
takeaways: ابدأ من نوع المتغير وعدد المتغيرات.
كل رسم له سؤال يناسبه وحدود يجب ذكرها.
المسار العربي يكرر المفاهيم بالعربية، وليس ترجمة حرفية.

lessons.title: الألوان في Data Visualization
takeaways: Qualitative للفئات، وSequential للمقدار المرتب.
Diverging يحتاج نقطة midpoint ذات معنى.
Viridis خيار عملي للـsequential.

lessons.title: نصائح عملية وبنك أسئلة
takeaways: اختيار الرسم داخل Power BI يبدأ من السؤال.
الأداء جزء من جودة التصور، وليس موضوعًا منفصلًا.
أجب عن أسئلة المقابلات بالـtrade-offs.

lessons.title: مسارات قراءة مقترحة
takeaways: اختر مسارًا واحدًا حسب الهدف: BI أو EDA أو مقابلات.
لا تكرر الفصول نفسها في كل مسار.
ابدأ من الأساسيات ثم انتقل للتطبيق.

lessons.title: مراجع مختارة
takeaways: احتفظ بالمصدر الأصلي لكل فكرة.
افصل بين مراجع الإدراك البصري والمراجع الإحصائية.
المرجع الجيد يشرح القيود، وليس فقط الأمثلة.
